intro.caption: Lesson 7-5 — the coordinate plane. Grimble sells bad maps because he keeps the REAL one locked in his vault, deep in the Map Room. The floor is a giant grid, and only the right tiles are safe. Three reader gates and a boss path stand between the Delvers and the map.

balloons.t: The floor is a coordinate plane. I'll plot the safe tiles one point at a time.
The fountain is the origin, (0, 0). Step ONLY on the tiles Sol plots.
First safe tile: (−1, 5). That's 1 left and 5 up.
I went 5 that way and 1 down. Same numbers! Right?

pages.caption: Kwame moved 5 right and 1 down. He stood on (5, −1), not (−1, 5). He swapped x and y. In an ordered pair, x (left or right) always comes first.

balloons.t: Start at the fountain every time. Left or right first. Then up or down.
Shh! He's asleep. Name each gem's spot quietly.
Little help? I think I swapped something.
Three tiles to the vault. Plot them right and the path lights up.
The real map! Every point plotted. Kwame only fell in once.

win.caption: An ordered pair (x, y) gives directions from the origin: x first, left or right; then y, up or down. Swapping them lands on a different point, often in a different quadrant.

gates.title: Gate 1 · Plot the Tiles
gates.prompt: The floor is a coordinate plane and the fountain is the origin, (0, 0). Plot each safe tile.
hints: Conceptual: in (x, y), the first number moves you left or right, and the second moves you up or down.
Procedural: start at the origin. Move x: right if positive, left if negative. Then move y: up if positive, down if negative.

steps: Start at the origin. x = −2, so move 2 units LEFT.
y = 3, so move 3 units UP. Mark the point.
worked.q: For (4, −1), which way do you move first?

fb.msg: You swapped x and y. x = −4 comes first: move LEFT 4. Then y = 2: up 2.
x is −4, so move LEFT from the origin, not right.
y is +2, so move UP, not down.

items.fbDefault: Start at (0, 0). Move 4 left, then 2 up.

fb.msg: You swapped x and y. x = 5 comes first: move RIGHT 5. Then y = −3: down 3.
y is −3, so move DOWN, not up.
x is 5, so move RIGHT from the origin.

items.fbDefault: Start at (0, 0). Move 5 right, then 3 down.

gates.pass: Two tiles glow gold under Anya's boots. Nobody falls in. Kwame claps from his hole.

gates.title: Gate 2 · Name the Spot
gates.badge: Spot Namer — Read Points and Quadrants
gates.prompt: Gems are scattered on the floor. Name where they are, quietly.
hints: Conceptual: left or right gives x, up or down gives y. The axes split the plane into four quadrants, numbered I to IV.
Procedural: write the left/right move first, with a minus sign for left. Then the up/down move, with a minus sign for down.

steps: x = 4 is positive (right). y = −2 is negative (down).
Right and down is Quadrant IV.

items.q: A ruby sits 3 left of the fountain and 6 up. Which ordered pair names it?

options.fb: That's x and y swapped. Left or right comes first, so x = −3.
Left means a negative x: −3, not 3.
Up means a positive y: 6, not −6.

items.q: An emerald is at (−2, −5). Which quadrant is it in?

options.fb: In Quadrant I, x and y are both positive. Here both are negative.
Quadrant II has negative x but positive y. Here y is negative too.
Quadrant IV has positive x and negative y. Here x is negative.

gates.pass: The ruby is at (−3, 6), the emerald in Quadrant III. Grimble snores on.

gates.title: Gate 3 · Fix the Swap
gates.prompt: Kwame was told (−1, 5). He stood on (5, −1) and the floor opened. Fix it.
hints: Conceptual: (−1, 5) and (5, −1) use the same numbers, but they are different points. Order matters.
Procedural: read the first number as left or right, and the second as up or down. Then plot.

steps: Practice: Bao was told (3, −2). He went 2 left and 3 up.
That is (−2, 3): he swapped the numbers.
Fix it: 3 right first, then 2 down. That is (3, −2).
worked.q: Kwame is told (0, 4). Does he move left or right at all?
worked.a: No. x = 0, so he only moves 4 up.

fb.msg: That's where Kwame stood: the swapped point. x = −1 comes first, so move 1 LEFT.
x is −1, so move left, not right.
y is 5, so move up, not down.

options.t: He started at the wrong spot
options.fb: He started at the fountain, (0, 0), which is right. The mistake came after.

options.t: He used the second number for left or right and the first for up or down
He only got the sign of 5 wrong
options.fb: He went 5 to the RIGHT, sideways. The 5 should have moved him UP. He swapped the two numbers.

gates.pass: Kwame climbs out and steps on (−1, 5). It glows. He does a tiny victory dance, very quietly.

gates.title: Boss Gate · Light the Path
gates.prompt: Three safe tiles lead to the vault. Plot them, then answer two last locks.
hints: Conceptual: x is always first, y second. A point with a 0 sits on an axis, not in a quadrant.
Procedural: for each pair, start at the origin, move x left or right, then move y up or down.

steps: x = −5: move 5 left. y = 0: do not move up or down.
The point sits on the x-axis.
worked.q: Name the point that is 2 left and 5 up from the center.

items.q: Lock 1 · Light the path: plot (2, 4), (−3, −1) and (0, −5).

fb.msg: (4, 2) is a swap of (2, 4). Move 2 right first, then 4 up.
(−1, −3) is a swap of (−3, −1). Move 3 left first, then 1 down.
(−5, 0) is a swap of (0, −5). x = 0 means no move sideways; just go 5 down.

items.fbDefault: Plot all three points, and only those. x first, then y.

items.q: Lock 2 · The last tile, (0, −5), sits on which line?

options.fb: On the x-axis, y = 0. Here x = 0, so the point is on the y-axis.

options.t: Neither, it is in Quadrant IV
options.fb: A point with a 0 coordinate sits on an axis, not inside a quadrant.

items.q: Lock 3 · The vault handle is 4 right and 3 down from the center. Which ordered pair names it?

options.fb: That is 4 left and 3 up, the opposite way. Right is positive x and down is negative y.
That swaps the numbers. x goes first: 4 right, then 3 down.
That is 4 left. Right means a positive x.

gates.pass: Three tiles blaze gold, (0, −5) on the y-axis, and the handle at (4, −3) turns. CLUNK. The vault is open.

journal.heading: Lesson 7-5 — what the Map Room taught us
rows: (x, y) gives directions from the origin, (0, 0). x first: left or right. Then y: up or down.
Negative x means left, negative y means down. (−4, 2) is 4 left and 2 up.
The axes cut the plane into four quadrants. (−2, −5) is in Quadrant III, left and down.
A point with a 0 sits on an axis: (0, −5) is on the y-axis.
(−1, 5) and (5, −1) are different points. Swapping x and y puts you on the wrong tile.
journal.quote: "x first. Then y. Then NO falling." — Kwame

teacher.suggested: Use during or after lesson 7-5 (Represent Rational Numbers on the Coordinate Plane) as one focused read. Whole-class on a projector, pairs on devices, or independent practice. It covers only this lesson: plotting and naming points with ordered pairs in all four quadrants, points on the axes.
standards: Understand a rational number as a point on the number line; extend number line diagrams and coordinate axes to represent points with negative number coordinates
